record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Find a sensible notion of quasi-local mass that appears in nontrivial theorems, for example a theorem asserting that if a 3-dimensional region of volume V has quasi-local mass above a threshold M0(V,...), then every spacetime containing that region must contain a trapped surface and hence a black hole.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Find a notion of quasi-local mass m_QL(Ω) assigned to bounded 3-dimensional spacelike regions Ω (with appropriate induced geometric data: a Riemannian metric, a second fundamental form, and matter fields satisfying the dominant energy condition) in 3+1-dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes solving the Einstein equations, with the following property. There should exist a function M_0(V, …) of the volume V = Vol(Ω) (and possibly of other geometric quantities of Ω such as diameter or boundary geometry) such that the following theorem holds:

If Ω is any such 3-dimensional region with Vol(Ω) = V and m_QL(Ω) > M_0(V, …), then every globally hyperbolic spacetime (M, g) satisfying the Einstein equations with dominant energy condition that contains Ω as a spacelike region must contain a closed trapped surface (a closed spacelike 2-surface in M whose two null mean curvatures are both negative), and hence, by the Penrose singularity theorem, must be future causally incomplete (contain a "black hole").

Problem: Construct such a quasi-local mass m_QL and prove a nontrivial trapped-surface-formation theorem of the above type, with an explicit threshold function M_0(V, …).
artifact.category_tag: Quasi-local mass and trapped surfaces in general relativity
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive notion of quasi-local mass currently appears in a theorem of the stated "volume + mass threshold ⇒ trapped surface" form. Existing results (e.g., Schoen–Yau hoop-type theorems, Khuri's inequalities, and Wang–Yau quasilocal mass studies) give related but partial trapped-surface formation criteria, typically involving concentration of matter or initial-data conditions rather than a clean quasi-local-mass threshold. Recent work on Einstein–Vlasov trapped-surface formation (2025) and quasilocal mass at marginally trapped surfaces shows continued activity but no resolution of the general problem.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-Local Mass and the Existence of Horizons
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions on quasi-local mass implying existence of horizons; partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Partial trapped-surface/horizon existence results in terms of quasilocal-type quantities exist but are not of the volume-threshold form requested.

status_evidence.title: Semi-Global Existence and Trapped Surface Formation for the Einstein-Vlasov System
status_evidence.snippet: Dynamical formation of trapped surfaces proven for Einstein–Vlasov without symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: Recent trapped-surface formation theorems use focused initial data, not a quasi-local mass threshold against volume.

status_evidence.title: Four lectures on quasi-local mass
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of competing definitions of quasi-local mass; no consensus definition.
status_evidence.claim: There is still no single accepted notion of quasi-local mass satisfying all desired properties.
